All legacy mcdonalds.com.au/sites/mcdonalds.com.au/files/*.pdf links now 302 to the home page. Product pages such as https://www.mcdonalds.com/au/en-au/menu/beef/big-mac.html render the nutrition panel by script, so WebFetch sees headers only. Direct download of the PDFs from this environment is blocked (www.mcdonalds.com is not on the session's network allowlist), so the tables could not be parsed locally. Fix options: open the PDFs or product pages in a real browser, or add www.mcdonalds.com to the allowed domains so the PDF can be downloaded and its tables read properly.
